miniLm.note: The live context router itself gives semantic classification roughly a 700 ms deadline; physical evidence should report actual cold and warm latency rather than substituting synthetic throttling.

evidenceRules.contentHash: SHA-256 over the exported evidence record before the evidenceHash field is attached
evidenceRules.memoryMeasurement: Use browser process/heap measurement when exposed. A manually observed OS/process peak may be supplied when the browser does not expose a usable memory API, but the evidence must identify it as manual.

operatorProtocol: Open the lab on the real low-end phone and capture the device snapshot.
Install the highly recommended MiniLM package and SmolLM2 135M test model if they are not already present.
Run automated core checks to cold-reset and time MiniLM, verify worker release/recovery, and perform direct 135M generation.
Arm offline relaunch, enable airplane mode, fully close Civweave, and reopen the same lab from the installed PWA.
Arm memory-pressure return, background Civweave, create realistic OS memory pressure using other apps, return, and attest only if the same run survived without reinstalling.
On a fresh or deliberately incomplete 135M download, arm the interruption checkpoint, close Civweave during visible progress, reopen, and resume to completion.
Record battery and thermal behavior after the physical run.
Export the hashed evidence JSON. Do not mark this matrix pass until every required scenario and measurement is present and the evidence has been reviewed.
policy: Physical evidence must come from a real low-end device. Synthetic CI and desktop throttling may supplement but cannot satisfy this gate. A pass requires every required scenario to complete without unrecoverable state loss, boot lockout, or a required reinstall. Thermal shutdown or visible thermal throttling is a failed thermal scenario.
